details.publicNotes:
When regret, guilt, and anger about an event that someone feels they could have stopped become strong enough, a lingering regret is born. They seek out the person whose feelings created them and do whatever it takes to "correct" the timeline. Though some creators appreciate the assistance, many are horrified by the lingering regret's willingness to commit atrocities in pursuit of their goals. For their part, lingering regrets are inclined to interpret any reticence their creators display as a sign that they need to go farther to prove the value of their methods.

Once defeated, lingering regrets rarely stay subdued forever. As long as their creators hold on to the feelings that gave them life, they will eventually return to continue their mission.

Shards of Time

Lingering regrets resemble younger versions of their creators, frequently looking and dressing exactly as they did during a particularly painful episode of the creator's life. Their appearance is a vivid reminder of the creator's past failures, and few people can bear to stare their lingering regrets in the face.

Besides their creators' peace of mind, lingering regrets are particularly destructive to one other type of object: mirrors. When a lingering regret sees their own reflection in a mirror, the mirror shatters.

You learn the direction to the target (if you picked a specific object, such as "my mother's sword") or the nearest target (if you picked a type of object, such as "swords"). If the target is a specific object, you must have observed it directly with your own senses. If it's a type of object, you still need to have an accurate mental image of the type of object. If there's lead or running water between you and the target, this spell can't locate the object. This means you might find a type of object farther away if the nearest one is behind lead or running water.

Heightened (5th) You can target a specific creature or ancestry instead of an object, but you must have met or seen up close the creature or ancestry you want to target.

target.value: 1 specific object or type of object
1 specific object or type of object, or a specific creature or ancestry

description.value:
You conjure up a wall of slowed time, which is both transparent and sepia-colored. The wall is 1 inch thick, up to 120 feet long, and up to 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically or be supported by any surface. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Mindless creatures, unattended objects (including thrown weapons and ammunition), and spell effects that pass through the wall are trapped within, emerging 1 round after they enter it. Held objects that enter the wall, such as a melee weapon used to Strike a creature on the other side of the wall, become stuck for 1 round as well. The creature can choose to drop the held object; if they do, the object continues its trajectory after it is freed from the wall's effect; this would allow a melee weapon to resolve the Strike before falling to the ground. However, attacks and targeted effects whose targets have moved from their original position since they entered the wall automatically miss.

Non-mindless creatures that enter the wall of time lose one action from their current turn if they can; if they can't, either because they are on their final action for the turn or it is not their turn, they are instead @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

You pull an echo of your target's recent injuries through time, inflicting them anew. Choose a type of damage that the target has taken since the beginning of your last turn. The target takes 2d6 damage of that type.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

target.value: 1 creature that has taken damage since the beginning of your last turn

description.value: lingering regrets can only exist in the past and react viscerally to being displaced in the future. Whenever a lingering regret is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened}, their body congeals. They gain no extra actions from being quickened, instead losing their resistance to all damage.

Trigger A creature within 60 feet of the lingering regret Steps or Strides

Effect The lingering regret launches the creature backward in time, returning it to the square it was in at the beginning of its Step or Stride unless it succeeds at a @Check[will|dc:26] save.

The lingering regret's negative emotions flare up as they slice into nearby creatures with fractured moments of time laden with their deepest sorrows. All creatures in a @Template[type:burst|distance:20] take @Damage[4d6[mental],3d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save). Squares in the burst are littered with broken shards of time, becoming difficult terrain for all creatures except the lingering regret until the beginning of the lingering regret's next turn. Creatures that end their turn in one of these squares must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:25] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from the rush of emotions they emit (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The lingering regret can't use Stagnant Sorrows again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Stagnant Sorrows]]{1d4 rounds}.

A creature that takes damage from a regret's caress or regret's lash Strike is shoved back into memories of moments it regrets. It must succeed a @Check[will|dc:25] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.
